newsitem.title: CANADA: Britain, Brazil selling planes for Canada training.
newsitem.headline: Britain, Brazil selling planes for Canada training.

text.p: Brazilian and British companies will be selling planes for use in a NATO training program in Canada, officials said on Wednesday.
Canada's Bombardier Inc will buy the planes from British Aerospace Plc and Empresa Brasilereira de Aeronautica S.A. (Embraer) and then provide the training and maintenance at Moose Jaw, Saskatchewan.
The program manager on the military side, Jim Richardson, said the total cost of the NATO program would be C$2 billion to C$3 billion over 25 years.
British Aerospace will supply up to 25 Hawk 100 jets, and Embraer will provide up to 27 of the more basic Super Tucanos, a high-end turbo-prop aircraft.
Pilots would start on the Super Tucanos and proceed to the Hawk 100s, which will enable them to proceed to more sophisticated jets flown by their militaries.
A Canadian government statement said the British, Danish and Norwegian air forces have expressed formal interest in participating, and the Canadian air force is also committed.
